Subject: Recap & next steps — private/VPC security intake (Equinox)

Hi Samantha / Paul,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the Equinox infra and security team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single action list to work from.

Key points from the call:
- Equinox wants a private/VPC deployment of Redwood (no public endpoints) with strict egress controls and optional air-gapped enclave for ML model updates.
- Primary compliance drivers: HIPAA for a subset of workloads, GDPR for EU data, and SOC 2 Type II is required for vendor acceptance.
- Equinox is ok with Redwood-managed control plane but requires KMS integration and audit log exports to their SIEM.

Immediate asks we captured:
1) Equinox to share the vendor security questionnaire (we can triage and return answers) — Samantha, you mentioned a standard third-party XLS.
2) Redwood to provide an initial network topology diagram that shows VPC peering, NAT/egress, and optional air-gapped data path.
3) SOC 2 status and expected audit timeline (where we are on Type I/II).
4) Clarify data-at-rest encryption (KMS/HSM options) and key custody models.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
- Redwood: Send vendor questionnaire and a template network diagram for review (Evelyn) — by EOD Monday 12/6.
- Equinox: Return completed questionnaire and an initial network constraints doc (Samantha) — by 12/10.
- Schedule a 60-minute architecture review with your infra/security engineers and Redwood's solutions + security (Ben & Karthik) — propose week of 12/13.

Attachments: none in this message — we'll attach the questionnaire in the next email.

If that lines up, I'll drop the questionnaire and a draft topology in the thread.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: (415) 555-0126

Evelyn — thanks for the summary and the clear next steps. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Vendor questionnaire: attaching our standard vendor security XLS here. It includes sections on SOC 2, encryption, network controls, incident response, and third-party subprocessor use. Please populate columns A-C if possible.
- SOC 2: Equinox requires vendors to be SOC 2 Type II or have a documented remediation plan + acceptance from our legal team. Our current procurement window expects evidence by Jan 2028 (ideally before final sign-off).
- HIPAA: Only a subset of our pipelines (PHI payloads) will be in scope; we need to understand Redwood's support for BAA and data segregation at the model/namespace level.

Quick clarifying questions for Redwood prior to the architecture review:
1) Can Redwood run in an air-gapped enclave where outbound internet access is fully restricted except for an operator-mediated model sync?
2) What KMS integrations do you support (Cloud KMS, AWS CloudHSM, key rotation cadence)?
3) Do you provide an auditable stream of per-request logs (with tokenized user IDs) that we can ingest into Splunk?

We're targeting 12/13–12/17 for the architecture review; would prefer afternoons PST.

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — private/VPC security intake (Equinox)

Samantha — thanks for sending the questionnaire. I've filled the first-pass answers in the attached workbook (EQX_redwood_answers.xlsx) — see the following highlights here inline:

- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report for our control plane covering change management, availability, and logging. The private deployment control plane for fully customer-managed installs is covered under our enterprise compliance program; we have a Type II audit planned for Feb 2028. I added the relevant pages and evidence pointers in the spreadsheet.
- Air-gapped enclaves: We support an air-gap mode for model payloads and KV cache syncs; model binaries can be staged via an operator-managed image bundle (no direct outbound egress required). There are tradeoffs on update cadence — documented in the questionnaire.
- KMS: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and can support CloudHSM-managed keys; for on-prem we support customer HSM with standard KMIP. Key rotation is customer-controlled; our SDKs honor rotation with zero-downtime rewrap where possible.
- Audit logs: We produce per-request audit logs with request IDs, timestamp, model id, and token counts. We can stream logs to customer S3/GCS or forward to a syslog/FluentD endpoint. We also support delivering logs via a webhook to your SIEM if required.

Attached: eqx_vendor_questionnaire_v1.xlsx (completed answers, redwood commentary)
Also attaching a draft topology (proposed_network_diagram_v1.png) showing a VPC-only deployment and an optional air-gapped training/update path.

Next step: Can Paul drop an initial list of their internal IP ranges and any appliance constraints? That will let us produce a final diagram that respects their private subnets and egress filters.

I'll also add Ben and Karthik to coordinate the architecture review scheduling. Proposed slots:
- Tue 12/14 1:00–2:00 PM PST
- Wed 12/15 3:00–4:00 PM PST

Best,
Evelyn

Evelyn / team — thanks for the detailed answers and the draft diagram. A few clarifications from infra:

1) We've attached our initial network constraints and a rough diagram of our current on-prem edge (see attachment). We're evaluating using a VPN + VPC peering model for connectivity to vendor-managed services.
2) For the air-gapped requirement: we need to confirm whether Redwood requires any outbound DNS/TLS for health checks if deployed in air-gap mode. Our security policy currently forbids outbound DNS/TLS from air-gapped enclaves without explicit exception.
3) HIPAA / BAA: legal will want language around data segregation per-tenant and minimum retention guarantees — can Redwood provide a draft BAA addendum ahead of the architecture review?

Attached: eqx_initial_network_constraints.pdf, eqx_onprem_edge_sketch.png

On scheduling, 12/14 1–2 PM PST works for our team.

For hybrid (reduced egress) we can enable limited egress to specific endpoints under a strict allowlist. We'll cover specifics in the call.
